The lattice parameters analyzed were geometry, dielectric contrast and size. The results can be readily applied in PBG technology devices design.

articleTitle: Spectral functional forms for modeling SOAs noise
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We discuss the applicability of a recently presented black box model for semiconductor optical amplifiers for the modeling of the amplifier's noise. We show that this BBM works if the ASE output power can be approximated by the equivalent input noise model. For this purpose we first rederive the BBM, showing the spectral functional forms used in it and its experimental validation.

articleTitle: A new time domain BPM based on locally one dimensional method
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper introduces a new approach for the scalar time domain beam propagation method (TD-BPM). The formalism is expanded in terms of a locally one dimensional (LOD) operator splitting technique, resulting in an improved computational efficiency. In addition, this approach also utilizes the Crank-Nicolson scheme, which makes it unconditionally stable.

articleTitle: Development of a testbed to intelligent systems on software defined radio
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The advances in wireless communication grew so much since the 90's, that a unique platform was required as a new alternative to this all portable devices. Therefore, this is not possible without using DSPs and FPGAs as a reconfigurable hardware. This tendency implicates in a new concept called software defined radio. In the University of Brasilia, there is a study group in SDR and its applications. This article will present the work done so far, as well as the difficulties that have to be surpassed in the process of developing of a software defined radio testbed.

articleTitle: Extinction ratio improvement using the regenerative properties of four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This work proposes a simple and efficient technique to improve the extinction ratio of a transmitter by using the regenerative properties of four-wave mixing (FWM) in a highly non-linear dispersion shifted fiber. We developed a theoretical model that shows the possibility of a 3 dB increase in the optical transmitter extinction ratio, which is an important design parameter. The numerical simulations confirm the theoretical model and reveal that there should be a trade-off among fiber and systems parameters to avoid eye closure penalty.

articleTitle: Convergence analysis of integral equations for characterization of RF channels
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The main concern of the present work is to investigate the convergence of the electric and magnetic field integral equations (EFIE and MFIE) adopted in the characterization of radio wave propagation over irregular terrains. The terrain irregularities are smooth, such that back-scattering is neglected and a recursive technique is used to determine the equivalent currents. Due to the near-grazing incidence and the vertical polarization of the incident field, the terrain can be considered an open surface made of a perfect magnetic conductor. This approach leads toward an equivalent problem that, in principle, can not be solved by the EFIE, a fact apparently overlooked in the literature. This may explain why the MFIE provides accurate results with a smaller number of basis functions than the EFIE.

articleTitle: Simulation of a optical burst switch using fiber delay lines
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Optical communication systems continues to play a significant role in the development of emerging network infrastructure. The areas of interest are focusing on optical networking for traditional telecommunications applications with emphasis on network and node design, traffic modeling and routing control and signaling, etc. An investigation of the performance of an optical burst switching (OBS) networks is described. Optical burst switching networks have received a lot of attention on the research community in the recent years. First the description of an OBS model created by implementation multiple single N-channel network models in the library public simulation IKRSimLib 2.5 is presented. The JET protocol, first proposed by Qiao and Yoo in 1997 is used for resource allocation in these simulation model. This is followed by an investigation of two models of arrival process of bursts are applied, form performance evaluation for delay and dropping probabilities. In particular, the performance of wavelength conversion has been evaluated under traffic load. We combined the optical burst switching with single FDL buffers to enhance system performance.

articleTitle: Experimental and simulation analysis of unbalanced Mach-Zehnder fiber Bragg grating OADM
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: An add/drop based in an all fiber Mach-Zehnder Interferometer and two identical fiber Bragg Gratings (MZ-FG) assembled with discrete components is investigated with experiments and simulation. The influence of the components parameters on undesirable power return is showed.

articleTitle: Modeling of a resonant tunneling diode optical modulator
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The integration of a double barrier resonant tunneling diode within a unipolar optical waveguide provides electrical gain over a wide bandwidth. Due to the nonlinearities introduced by the double barrier resonant tunneling diode an unipolar InGaAlAs/InP optical waveguide can be employed both as optical modulator and optical detector. The modeling results of a device operating as optical modulator agree with preliminary experimental data, foreseeing for an optimized device modulation depths up to 23 dB with chirp parameter between -1 and 0 in the wavelength range analyzed (1520 nm - 1600 nm).

articleTitle: A simple thermal model for predicting wavelength modulation dynamics in VCSELs
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: A simple thermal model for VCSELs is proposed, and tested in the task of predicting the dynamic behavior of wavelength variation with current. This effect is used in an optoelectronic setup to produce a nonlinear map from input voltage to detected optical signal. Since the effect is thermal in nature, the overall nonlinear relation changes with signal frequency. The model is shown to predict the shape of the nonlinear map in frequencies from kilohertz to megahertz, and is simple enough to be used in the simulation of large arrays.

articleTitle: The Weaver theoretical approach to generate some important TV digital signals for the transmission systems
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Nowadays many research centers around the entire world have been concentrating their efforts to discover what is the more convenient digital transmission system that can substitute appropriately that conventional analog one, which for many years were used and reached a very sophisticate technology. In front of this very important demanded question, a great number of telecommunication companies have been acquiring a large experience to modeling, implementing and testing efficient transmission equipments. Besides of the technological background demanded in the implementation of actual modern electronic architectures, it takes an important hole to adopt an appropriate way for the modeling. The main purpose of this paper is to present an accurate way to generate a class of important digital signals, like the SSB, VSB 8-VSB by using the Weaver method as the fundamental theoretical tool.

articleTitle: Indoor and outdoor evaluation of missile prototype scattering diagrams
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Radar cross section (RCS) measurements allow the equivalent area of a target when illuminated by radar to be determined. In other words, the RCS is the ratio between the energy of an electromagnetic wave emitted by radar that impinges on a target and the energy scattered by it. The scattering measurements can be performed monostatically, whereby the electromagnetic waves reflected by the target are measured in the same direction as the emitting source (radar), or by the bistatic method, when the reflected waves are captured in other directions. This article discusses the preliminary work currently being developed at AMR/IAE/CTA, involving the characterization of RAM (radar absorbing materials) applied on a target with complex geometry. In this particular study a missile prototype was used. The methodologies employed here are based on a closed-field (indoor) RCS range, using an anechoic chamber, and an open-field (outdoor) RCS range, both in the X-band frequency range

articleTitle: Synthesize of multilayer passive structures using genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: In this paper genetic algorithms were used in order to synthesize dielectric multilayer and symmetric passive structures with plane interfaces, considering TEM waves with normal and oblique incidences. The genetic algorithm optimization objective is to obtain each layer thickness to get a suitable filter response related to scattering parameters. The implemented algorithm codes were created in Matlab software in a very flexible manner to permit the designer specifies algorithm parameters and physical characteristics of the structure considered. Results and analysis of the algorithm configuration and efficiency are shown. Comparison with another optimization method and frequency response variance with the number of layers and incidence angles are also presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of hybrid WDM/OCDM networks with all-optical code converters
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: In this work, optical networks using the hybrid technology of wavelength division multiplexing and optical code division multiplexing (WDM/OCDM) with all-optical code converters are investigated. Expressions to show the code converter node performance including the effects of polarization mode dispersion (PMD) are derived. The main results show that the effects of PMD can decrease the code converter performance. It is also investigated a simple analytical formalism to solve the problem of optimal code converter placement. This formalism shows the network performance when the code converter are optimally/uniformly distributed in the network.

articleTitle: Characteristics of electromagnetic radiation absorption in plain coverings with ferrite Mg-Mn
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The production technology of covering electromagnetic radiation absorbers of the blanket type is related with the development of new materials and its electromagnetic properties. In this paper it is presented a methodology of one layer plain covering production, with absorption characteristics tuned in the frequency of 9 GHz. These coverings have been confectioned joining ferrite powder of Mg-Mn with aliphatic resin with base epoxy. Reflectivity measurements have been carried out in three samples with different compositions, in the 8 to 12 GHz frequency range, to study its electromagnetic radiation absorption characteristics. The reflectivity data are presented and compared between the different samples.

articleTitle: Bandstop response of microstrip lines with defected ground structures
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: A fast and direct method to estimate the stopband in microstrip lines with periodic defected ground structures (DGS) is introduced in this paper. Based on the equivalent circuit of single DGS unit, an approximate relationship between the stopband and DGS circuit dimensions is set up. Comparison between the estimated results and simulated results based on field analysis methods verifies the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fully-integrated dual-standard BiFET low-noise amplifier for DCS1800/WCDMA applications
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a fully-integrated dual-standard BiFET low noise amplifier (LNA) targeted to DCS1800 (1805-1880 MHz) and WCDMA-FDD (2110-2170 MHz) systems applications. It uses a high performance 0.25-/spl mu/m SiGe:C BiCMOS7RF integration technology. The main motivation of this work is to share as many elements as possible in both modes avoiding conventional parallel LNAs, which is not a cost-efficient solution. In DCS1800 mode, the LNA S21 is 14.9 dB (250 MHz -1 dB bandwidth), NF is 1.47 dB, ICP1 and IIP3 are -12 dBm and -2 dBm, respectively. In WCDMA mode, the LNA achieves a power gain of 15.5 dB (340 MHz -1 dB bandwidth), a NF of 1.49 dB, an ICP1 and IIP3 of -14 dBm and -4 dBm, respectively. It consumes 6.6 mW in both operation modes, under 2.2 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Improving the efficiency of an evolutionary algorithm in the optimization of analog microwave circuits using regularized RBF networks
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a simple approach used to speed up the convergence of an evolutionary optimizer. It uses regularized radial basis functions networks in order to model the objective-function and to provide an inexpensive simulation model used to estimate good solutions. We empirically show that this hybrid method is capable to offer qualitative jumps along the search process. The method is especially appropriate to the optimization of nonlinear analog microwave circuits with costly simulations, since the number of required evaluations and the overall time to achieve a solution is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Smart antenna system using five-port reflectometer
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The difficult design of variable phase shifters for smart antenna applications makes digital beamforming systems an interesting way for future communication systems that aim to provide better network performance. Five-port reflectometers use a third redundant mixer to decrease the system dependency from the phase and amplitude unbalance of local oscillators. We introduce a digital beamforming system for reception array using the five-port technique which performs a direct conversion of RF signals. The system performance is tested by measuring its bit error rate for different number of antenna array elements.

articleTitle: A novel and efficient time domain full-band method for photonics applications
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, a new time-domain numerical approach for two-dimension vectorial wave equation solutions based on slow wave variation is presented. The algorithm incorporates finite element discretization and uses orthogonal edge basis functions to describe pulse propagation in optical waveguides.

articleTitle: Reentrant cylindrical cavities
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Of applications ranging from electron spin resonance to detection of gravitational waves, reentrant cylindrical cavities are analyzed on the basis of a mathematically simple formalism extending the range of validity of expressions for resonant frequency and quality factor obtained from lumped RLC constant models. Several cavity configurations in the 1-3 GHz range are analytically examined in excellent agreement with frequencies obtained from Superfish code.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics in straight open-groove structures
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents the propagation characteristics in straight open-groove structures in UHF based on the imperfect waveguide method. The attenuation constant due to surrounding media absorption, sidewalls tilt and the roughness of the sidewalls are considered and corrected. Numerical results are presented for the attenuation constant. These results show that the losses due to the roughness of the sidewalls are inversely proportional to the frequency and losses due to sidewalls tilt is the main cause of power loss at high frequencies. Thus attenuation due to absorption and roughness of the sidewalls are negligible in comparison to attenuation due to sidewalls tilt in this frequency range.

articleTitle: Coupling coefficients of combline resonators
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Bandpass filters require elements that behave as series or parallel resonant circuits. In this paper, we discuss a variety of couplings between combline resonators in bandpass filter applications. Coupling coefficient used in filter realizations has been precisely calculated. Filter responses are presented by simulation, experiment and calculation. They were in very good agreement.

articleTitle: Applying optical coherence tomography in dental restoration
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Optical coherence tomography was use to perform an evaluation of molar dental restorations. Imaging resolution of 10 /spl mu/m is achieved and dental cavities small as 50 /spl mu/m are measured. OCT images were compared with X-ray and optical microscopy pictures.

articleTitle: Heating reproducibility in microwave chemistry
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Statistically designed heating experiments were performed using different microwave sources to heat water under identical operating conditions. Three 2.45 GHz microwave generators were used: a) a 800 W maximum variable power source utilizing a domestic oven model magnetron; b) a 3 kW maximum non-filtered variable power commercial generator and c) a 2 kW maximum low-ripple variable power commercial generator. The same volume of water was successively heated utilizing the three different microwave sources, with equal effective power levels ranging from 190 to 380 W. The energy absorbed by the water load was evaluated by measuring the temperature increase. Preliminary results indicate that heating efficiency may vary with the type of microwave source.

articleTitle: Employing engineering methods for the analysis of OLEDs
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We analyze typical static curves of organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs) that were obtained under mid-to-high biases, leading to forward currents ranging from contact-limited regime of injection to bulk-limited transport of majority carriers. We also present arguments to suggest that our OLEDs effectively behave as Schottky devices under static electric characterization. Two engineering methods, usually applied for inorganic Schottky diodes analysis, are shown to be also suitable for evaluation of OLEDs. As an alternative approach impedance spectroscopy measurements are employed to confirm that a Schottky-like type of behavior is adequate for modeling of OLEDs.

articleTitle: 4 /spl times/ 20 Gb/s L-band NRZ signal transmission through a metro-scaled NZD fiber link
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We describe an L-band WDM error-free transmission over 50 km of nonzero dispersion-shifted fiber, at a per-channel rate of 20 Gb/s. By allocating an equally spaced 4-channel optical stream close to the fiber zero-dispersion wavelength, and transmitting them in a linear regime, no dispersion-compensating module is required and no four-wave mixing effect is observed. Except for the lithium niobate modulator and the O/E receiver bandwidths, all system elements have been previously specified for 10 Gb/s L-band WDM transmissions. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of upgrading a system capacity by combining the L-band amplification with a dispersion shifted fiber, and a linear-regime transmission at a bit-rate of 20 Gb/s, which is less technologically restringing and complex than 40 Gb/s. The strategy of reducing the need for new components and reusing the legacy equipment may represent a significant cost impact in a metro-scaled system upgrade.

articleTitle: A new spatio-temporal 2D-FEM formulation applied to optical devices with cylindrical symmetry
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: A new and efficient spatio-temporal formulation based on the finite element method 2D is applied to simulate optical devices with cylindrical symmetry. One spatial coordinate r, radial component, and one temporal coordinate /spl tau/, transversal component, constitute the discretization domain. The propagation occurs along z-direction, being incremented by Crank-Nicholson scheme. The finite-element in conjunction with Galerkin's method it's been applied to discretizate the transversal domain and perfect matched layers (PML's) are placed to truncate the transversal boundaries.

articleTitle: Spectral correlations of PMD variables in optical fibers
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: A simulation tool for the calculation of the statistics and correlations of PMD-related variables is presented. Calculations are performed in time domain, allowing the simulation of the temporal evolution of differential group delay (DGD), principal states of polarization, (PSP) output polarization state (SOP) among others. Results are in good agreement with predictions from spectral calculations. Correlations between neighboring channels in a 100 GHz spaced WDM transmission falls down rapidly for PMD values above 4 ps.

articleTitle: The shelter of high energy electrons produced by the powerful HF transmitter
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: It is possible in southern hemisphere countries develop together one scientific program aimed at studying the properties and behavior of the ionosphere based on ground HF power transmitted radiation. The goal of this work is to further advance in knowledge of the physical and electrical properties of the Earth's ionosphere plasma, which can affect mostly communication and navigation systems and weather change. We describe here research instruments facilities for southern hemisphere and also plasma calculations for Antarctica. The main ionospheric research apparatus consist in a high power HF transmitter that can be used temporally to excite a limited area of the ionosphere for scientific studies. The question is: what is the greatest energy of ionospheric electrons until they could be accelerated by electromagnetic radiation of power HF transmitter.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of an wavelength/code-routed burst switched network
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper analysis the use of hybrid technology of wavelength division multiplexing and optical code division multiplexing (WDM/OCDM) for optical burst switching (OBS) with two-way reservation scheme. The architecture of WDM/OCDM edge router that utilizes fast circuit switching by dynamically assigning and releasing virtual optical code/wavelength path channels (VOCP/VWP) over bufferless optical core is described. We derived expressions for burst blocking probability for the edge router and analyzed the behavior of the network in function the traffic load and latency. The main results show that are decreasing the burst blocking probability and network latency when increase the number of codes per wavelength.

articleTitle: Effects of PMD on hybrid WDM/OCDM networks
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper analyses the effects of polarization mode dispersion (PMD) on the blocking probability performance of optical networks that uses the hybrid technology of wavelength division multiplexing and optical code division multiplexing (WDM/OCDM). In these networks virtual paths based on code/wavelength channels (VCP/VWP) are dynamically established to attend the traffic demand. We use a routing channel assignment (RCA) based on genetic algorithm to established the VCP/VWP's. The main results show that the network blocking probability caused by PMD depends on parameters of optical orthogonal codes (OOC) like weight and length.

articleTitle: Symmetry properties of 2D magnetic photonic crystals with square lattice
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We consider possible magnetic symmetries of 2D square lattices with circular ferrite rods magnetized by a uniform DC magnetic field. These structures can be used as tunable and non-reciprocal photonic crystals. Classification of eigenmodes in such crystals and compatibility relations are defined on the basis of magnetic group theory and the theory of representations. Some general electromagnetic properties of the magnetic crystals such as change in the basic domain of the Brillouin zone, bidirectionality and nonreciprocity, symmetry restrictions for the electromagnetic waves and lifting of eigenwave degeneracies by the DC magnetic field are also discussed.

articleTitle: Ultra high frequency electromagnetic field effects in erythrocytes micronuclei frequency and birth rate of rats prenatally irradiated
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: An in vivo mammalian cytogenetic test, the micronuclei (MN) assay, was used to investigate the occurrence of genetic damage in rat offspring erythrocytes exposed to a non-thermal electromagnetic field (834 MHz, 0.6 - 1.4 W/kg) from a cellular phone during their embryogenesis. The irradiated group showed a significant increase of MN frequency. The offspring number has not been significantly different between the irradiated and sham groups. It could be concluded that selected UHF-EMF under the applied conditions direct or indirectly induced genotoxic response in hematopoiesis during the embryogenesis after whole-body exposure

articleTitle: The relationship between Mn-Zn ferrites with different iron ion contents and the absorption energy in X-band
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Ferrites of (Mn+Zn)/sub 1-x/Fe/sub 2+x/O/sub 4+/spl delta// type can be used in space, aeronautical, telecommunication and medical fields, due to their high magnetic permeability and low magnetic losses. This work intends to correlate the Mn/Zn and Fe/(Mn+Zn) ratios of these ferrites with the absorption of energy in the frequency range of 8.0 to 12.0 GHz. Considering this purpose, this work evaluates the absorption of energy of ferrites of (Mn+Zn)/sub 1-x/Fe/sub 2+x/O/sub 4+/spl delta// - type for x = -0.1; 0; 0.05; 0.1; 0.2. Ten samples were prepared maintaining the molar fraction of zinc oxide constant at 18% and 25%. The samples were prepared by conventional ceramic technique. The characterization was performed by reflectivity measurements using the waveguide technique.

articleTitle: Rain attenuation measurements at 23 and 38 GHz in convergent links in a tropical region
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Point-to multipoint links, using the emerging Wi-Max (worldwide interoperability microwave for access) technology and operating at frequencies in SHF band is subjected to severe attenuation by rainfall. Experimental measurements of rainfall rate and rain attenuation cumulative distributions, as presented in this paper, are necessary to enlarge the data bank of measures in tropical climates, aiming at the modelling for the effects of precipitation in individual and convergent radio links.

articleTitle: Modeling and design for an electrooptic directional coupler modulator
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: A numerical model is presented for an electrooptic directional coupler modulator. The model depends on the analysis of simple coplanar uniform electrodes. The analysis is based on the transverse resonance technique. An equivalent circuit is deduced to represent the structure of the modulator. General trial quantities are introduced as virtual adjustable sources in the equivalent circuit. It was observed that it is possible for such a device to be optimized by the variation of a number of fabrication parameters. The applied field and the change in optical waveguides optical field due to the antisymmetric refractive index change are calculated for the structure. Finally, the product of switching voltage and coupling length and optical loss due to the metal electrodes are also investigated.

articleTitle: Tunable filter interrogation method with a modulated fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This work describes the use of a mechanically modulated fiber Bragg grating to address a single fiber Bragg grating sensor using the tunable filter method. A special mechanical apparatus driven by a small PZT device is devised and fabricated to implement the tunability of the interrogating element which is another fiber Bragg grating that can be modulated and stretched to scan the spectral range of operation of the sensor.

articleTitle: An all-optical gain controlled EDFA using a fast variable optical attenuator
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The design and characterization of an all-optical gain controlled erbium doped fiber amplifier using an embedded variable optical attenuator in the feedback loop is presented. The gain (16-23 dB) is controlled by the attenuation level with high equalization (lower than 0.8 dB in all C band), low noise figure (around 5.3 dB), and absence of relaxation oscillations.

articleTitle: Optical transparent IP/WDM network simulation
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This work presents an optical transparent IP/WDM network simulation in mesh architecture. The implemented software allows the characterization of the transport, control and management planes of the network. The centralized vision of the control and management planes has the purpose economy of resource and time performance. The system, except for the control plane, was developed with public tools and can be modified and improved on the terms of GPL (GNU Public License).

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics of over-layered planar transmission line transformers
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: An over-layered planar transmission line transformer obtained by deposition of high dielectric constant thin films over the conductors printed on alumina substrates is proposed. The resulting effective dielectric constant becomes very high, dispersion is very low, and the cutoff frequency of higher order modes is significantly increased. The theoretical behavior of this device was investigated using the simulator HP-HFSS and the results were compared to those obtained for a coplanar transmission line transformer printed on conventional bulk substrate with relative dielectric constant of 80

articleTitle: Designing fiber dispersion for broadband parametric amplifiers
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We present a method to determine the fiber chromatic dispersion curve that optimizes the gain bandwidth and ripple of fiber optical parametric amplifiers. We found that controlling high order dispersion terms a great enhancement of the gain spectrum is achieved. We provide a simulation example of a photonic crystal fiber, designed to control up to the sixth order dispersion parameter that gives 33 dB of gain from 1440 nm to 1600 nm, within 0.2 dB of gain variation.

articleTitle: Visible light generation in semiconductor nano-pillars
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We report a calculation of the two first energy levels of semiconductor nano-pillars as a function of their diameters. We have considered GaAs and InAs self-assembled quantum dots disk-like shape. The region where the visible light is emitted was delimited. Encapsulating quantum dots with diameters from this region allows the fabrication of white light-emitting diodes.

articleTitle: Slot resonator with PBG layers
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper shows the study and results of the three layers slot resonator using photonic band gap (PBG) substrate. The full wave transverse transmission line (TTL) method is used to calculate the complex resonant frequency, using double spectral variables. This method presents efficient and concise calculus in the determination of the structure parameters. Numerical results for the resonant frequency of three layer's substrate slot antenna, for s and p polarization of PBG material, for different substrate thickness and resonator length are presented.

articleTitle: Microwave filter synthesis using mutation-driven evolutionary algorithm
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a mutation-driven evolutionary algorithm applied to microwave filter synthesis. In this approach the topologies of the circuits are completely defined during the evolution process, without any knowledge of traditional design strategies. The process uses models (building blocks) and insertion rules to place moderate constraints and reduce the size of the search space. The results show that the method is capable to generate circuits that meet the specifications. The synthesis capabilities are demonstrated using bandstop filters.

articleTitle: On the development of a higher-order PML
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: A new formulation based on stretched coordinates is developed for perfectly matched layers (PML). The new PML can have multiple poles in contrast to the regular PML with a single pole. The implementation is also derived and the preliminary results are shown to be better than the regular PML with insignificant increase in the computational cost.

articleTitle: Highly birefringent photonic crystal fiber with squeezed hexagonal and rectangular lattices
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The birefringence of photonic crystal fiber (PCF) with squeezed hexagonal and rectangular lattices was calculated by a finite element software. Squeezes in the x and y directions were taken into account considering an elliptical microstructure of holes. High values for the birefringence could be reached: 2.0/spl times/10/sup -2/ and 7.5/spl times/10/sup -3/ for hexagonal and rectangular lattices, respectively.

articleTitle: Power splitters for ultralow refractive index metallic nanostructures waveguides
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We investigated power splitters in air core waveguides with a metallic photonic crystal cladding. The mechanism of propagation in these guides is the total external reflection. The cladding is formed by a periodic arrangement of metallic wires on square or triangular lattices. Power splitters can be designed by modifying the geometry at the splitting region by introducing a reflecting structure in order to increase the transmission coefficient. Some splitters based on these structures are analyzed by an efficient frequency domain finite element approach.

articleTitle: Vectorial finite element BPM scheme applied to coupled leaky waveguide
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, an efficient finite-element formulation for dielectric media with transverse anisotropy is applied to the analysis of polished-type optical fiber couplers. The method uses triangular elements in the discretization and perfectly matched layers are used as absorbing boundary. In this case we assume that two cores are curved in a parabolic shape, and between them a leaky waveguide with an index-matching liquid layer is included. The distance between cores is variable parameters. Due the inclusion of leaky waveguide the coupling distance reduces drastically.

articleTitle: Optimizing conversion efficiency of the monotron, a microwave tube with RF-field bunching
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: In its classical embodiment - a circular cylindrical cavity driven by a rectilinear electron beam - the simplest of the transit-time microwave tubes, the monotron, has its conversion efficiency limited to 20.0%. But we demonstrate here that on considering a stepped electric-field axial profile described by a tanh(z) function, the monotron efficiency can attain the theoretical maximum value of 57.0%, almost three times as high as that obtained from the conventional uniform field distribution. This is accomplished by using two cavities electromagnetically coupled by an annular slit crossed by an electron stream. From a one-dimensional analysis, a two-cavity monotron is developed to operate in the TM/sub 010/ mode at 4.0 GHz when self-excited by a 20 keV, 10 A hollow electron beam. The device operation is examined through a 21/2-D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation giving a 47.5% conversion efficiency. Departure from the theoretically predicted efficiency is explained by beam-thickness effects.

articleTitle: Signal sampling method for power measurements in mobile UHF environments
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper depict. a measurement method that was developed to consistently characterize a mobile environment on the UHF band in terms of path loss. An automated data acquisition method is presented which consists of setting the sampling rate based on: a Rayleigh statistical distribution of the radio channel, the sounding instruments limitations and the intended mobile top speed. The Doppler effect is also taken into account when the resolution bandwidth is set. The paper also covers the acquired data processing technique that leads to the separation of the long and short term fading components using a moving mean filter.

articleTitle: Passive GaAs FET mixer architectures for ultra high linearity requirements
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper describes single-balanced passive GaAs FET mixers with different balancing principles for the lower GHz range. The mixers achieve conversion losses of about 7 dB and input third-order intercept points (IIP3) of up to 44 dBm. Different balancing topologies, design process and results are being discussed.

articleTitle: 2/spl times/10 Gb/s and 6 /spl times/GbE field trial transmission over Project GIGA Testbed
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: We report the first 8-channel error-free transmission at 10 Gb/s (2-channel) and GbE (6-channel) performed on Project GIGA Testbed. The 10 Gb/s 2-channel transmission performance has been characterized, in Campinas, in terms of Q-factor and bit-error-ratio (BER) as a function of receiver sensitivity and received optical signal-to-noise ratio, OSNR. The use of different schemes for dispersion compensation has been evaluated, as well as the impact of channel detuning.

articleTitle: Hybrid model of traffic characterization for optimization in GMPLS optical networks
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid traffic model for GMPLS (generalized multi-protocol label switched) optical networks. The model is focused in multi-service traffic characterized as self-similar and is used to produce more accurate QoS (quality of service) metrics which influence the different hierarchies of the network topology. Also, the model is used to implement an optimization procedure with a genetic algorithm for the establishment of link capacities in different physical mediums. The extensions of the model for the hierarchies of LSPs (label switched paths) in the GMPLS suite are also analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamic characteristics of rainfall rate in the Amazon Region and their effects on satellite link design
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper deals with an investigation of dynamic characteristics of rainfall rate in the Amazon Region. Experimental data from 3 (three) selected locations pertaining to different climate subtypes identified in this tropical rainy region constitute the basis of the analysis carried out here. Details about the annual clock hourly rainfall accumulation and the average duration of rainfall events are presented, the relevance of their effects in satellite system design being pointed out.

articleTitle: Modulation schemes for frequency coded quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: Frequency coding has been presented as a new alternative for qubits transmission on QKD systems. In this work we present an analysis of the different possibilities for modulation (amplitude or phase) in face of the BB84 and B92 protocols within systems employing frequency coding. It will be shown that schemes employing phase modulation both at Alice and Bob (PM-PM) are equivalent, in the sense that the classical BB84 protocol cannot be applied, to schemes using solely amplitude modulation (AM-AM). We present a new modulation scheme employing a combination of phase and amplitude modulation (AM-PM) which can accommodate classical BB84.

articleTitle: Analysis of different pumping schemes in distributed Raman amplifiers
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This work analyzes co, counter and bidirectionally pumped distributed Raman amplifiers (DRA) utilizing single mode fibers (SMF). Power and Signal analysis are employed to obtain important design parameters as gain, noise figure and eye penalties, and comparisons are made between the different configurations.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of polarization diversity gains for 1.8 GHz GSM downlink signals
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents an experimental evaluation of polarization diversity gains obtained for GSM downlink signals in the 1.8 GHz band. Data were acquired with a portable two-branch receiver, developed to include a signals selection diversity method, which was displaced at walking speed inside buildings featuring a variety of room sizes. The experimental setup and relevant environmental conditions pertaining to data collection are herein described. Diversity gains cumulative distribution functions resulting from raw data processing are analyzed.

articleTitle: A practical application of the finite element method and parallel computing to modeling UTP cable
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a practical application of the finite element method (FEM) in modeling the unshielded twisted pair (UTP) cable. The FEM was applied with a massively parallel processing (MPP) IBM RS/6000 SP computer. Three programs are presented: one for preprocessing, one for processing, and the other for post-processing.

articleTitle: 2005 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IEEE Cat. No.05TH8832C)
publicationTitle: SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave and Optoelectronics, 2005.
abstract: The following topics were dealt with: microstrip lines; surface-plasmon waves; photonics; optical communication; waveguide; antennas; receiver front-end; microwave tubes; radio networks; signal processing; optical fibers; semiconductor devices; and integrated circuits.
